Comprehensive Imprinting Analysis for a Sample Cohort

Source: R/module_scoring.R
AnalyzeImprintStatus.Rd

Computes maternal/paternal medians, IDS, angle, mechanism, status, and confidence per sample for a selected probeset. Supports both legacy beta/meta inputs and object-first ImprintomeSet input.

Usage

AnalyzeImprintStatus(
  betaFile,
  metaFile,
  probeset = probeset_options,
  ids_cutoff = 0.2,
  genome = "hg38",
  dmr_type = NULL,
  reference = c("auto", "controls", "fixed"),
  reference_group = NULL,
  reference_samples = NULL,
  reference_beta = NULL,
  infinium_type = c("all", "I", "II", "balanced"),
  balance = c("probe", "icr"),
  min_probes = 3L,
  n_boot = 0L,
  n_perm = 0L,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  resample = c("icr", "probe"),
  permute = c("icr", "probe"),
  resample_reference = FALSE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

betaFile

Data frame/matrix or file path containing probe-by-sample beta values, or an ImprintomeSet object.

metaFile

Metadata data frame or file path. Must be provided unless betaFile is an ImprintomeSet.

probeset

Character scalar naming a probeset key.

ids_cutoff

Numeric scalar threshold used to call imprinting alteration by IDS.

genome

Genome build of the probeset annotation, "hg19" or "hg38" (default "hg38"). Ignored when betaFile is an ImprintomeSet, whose own genome is used.

dmr_type

DMR_type values to score:

  • NULL (default): the panel default. The core selected panel is scored on gametic ICRs only ("gametic"); every other panel, and any panel without a DMR_type column, is scored on all probes.

  • "all": all probes, including secondary DMRs (the earlier default for selected).

  • one or more DMR_type values, for example "gametic" or "secondary" (secondary DMRs reported separately). Requires a DMR_type column in the probeset.

The dmr_type output column records the selection that was applied.

reference

How the balanced reference state is defined.

  • "auto" (default): use control samples when they are supplied, either external (reference_beta) or in-cohort (reference_group/ reference_samples). Fall back to the fixed 0.5 only when no controls are given, or when fewer than 3 are available (with a warning).

  • "controls": require a control reference; too few controls is an error.

  • "fixed": always use 0.5, the original behaviour.

With controls, each probe's reference is the median beta of that probe across the controls. Paternal and maternal deviations are medians of beta - reference, and IDS and Angle are computed from these deviations instead of from median - 0.5.

reference_group

Optional Sample_Group value(s) whose samples form an in-cohort control reference. Each control is itself scored against the other controls (leave-one-out).

reference_samples

Optional character vector of in-cohort control sample names, used instead of reference_group.

reference_beta

Optional external control reference, used when the cohort has no (or too few) controls. It can be one of:

  • a probe-by-sample beta matrix or data frame;

  • a beta file path;

  • a per-probe profile from BuildReferenceProfile(), given as the object or as an .rds path.

It should match the cohort's tissue, array type and preprocessing. Probes absent from the reference are dropped.

infinium_type

Infinium probe design types to score:

  • "all" (default): all probes;

  • "I" or "II": only that design type;

  • "balanced": compute each parental-class deviation separately within type I and type II probes, then average them.

Anything other than "all" requires an INFINIUM_DESIGN_TYPE column in the probeset.

balance

How probes are pooled into each parental class:

  • "probe" (default): the median over all probes of the class, so that probe-rich ICRs weigh more;

  • "icr": ICR-balanced, the median within each ICR (see AnalyzeICRStatus()) followed by the median across the class's ICRs, so that each ICR counts once. Requires an ICR_name column; probes outside annotated ICRs are not used. Cannot be combined with infinium_type = "balanced".

min_probes

Minimum number of probes for an ICR to count when balance = "icr" (default 3).

n_boot

Number of bootstrap replicates for confidence intervals of IDS and Angle (default 0, none). Several hundred to a few thousand are typical.

n_perm

Number of permutations for the parental-label null of the origin contrast (default 0, none). Use it only with a control reference (see Uncertainty).

conf_level

Confidence level of the bootstrap intervals (default 0.95).

resample

Bootstrap resampling unit within each parental class:

  • "icr" (default): two-stage cluster bootstrap. ICRs are resampled with replacement, then probes within each drawn ICR, so that correlated probes of one ICR are not treated as independent. Probes outside annotated ICRs count as their own cluster, and a class with a single ICR (for example IC1 or IC2 of chr11p15) reduces to resampling its probes. Requires an ICR_name column; otherwise "probe" is used, with a message.

  • "probe": probes are resampled within the class (within Infinium design types for infinium_type = "balanced", within ICRs for balance = "icr"). This ignores within-ICR correlation and gives narrower intervals.

permute

Permutation unit for the null:

  • "icr" (default): whole ICRs are reassigned; requires at least two annotated ICRs in each parental class. Always used with balance = "icr". With a paternal and b maternal ICRs there are only choose(a + b, a) distinct assignments, which bounds the smallest attainable p-value; a warning is given below 100. When the default cannot be used (a panel with one ICR per class, such as chr11p15), the test falls back to "probe" with a warning;

  • "probe": the parental labels of probes are shuffled, keeping the numbers of paternal and maternal probes (per design type for infinium_type = "balanced"). Correlated probes are exchanged individually, so p-values are anti-conservative.

resample_reference

With n_boot > 0 and in-cohort controls (reference_group or reference_samples), also resample the controls in each replicate and recompute the reference from them (each control again leave-one-out), so the intervals include the uncertainty of the reference itself. Default FALSE holds the reference fixed. Ignored, with a message, for the fixed 0.5 or an external reference.

seed

Optional random seed for n_boot/n_perm, for reproducible results; the caller's random number stream is restored afterwards.

Value

Data frame with sample-level imprinting metrics and labels. paternal_deviation and maternal_deviation are the coordinates that IDS and Angle are computed from. reference and n_reference_samples describe the reference used. balance records the pooling; with balance = "icr", the columns n_paternal_icrs / n_maternal_icrs give the numbers of ICRs used. With n_boot > 0, the columns IDS_lower, IDS_upper, Angle_lower, Angle_upper, Mechanism_support, n_boot, resample and resample_reference are added, and Status_interval: "above cutoff" (IDS_lower >= ids_cutoff), "below cutoff" (IDS_upper < ids_cutoff) or "borderline" (the interval spans the cutoff); with n_perm > 0, origin_perm_p, n_perm and permute (see Uncertainty). Calibrate the IDS cutoff on controls with CalibrateIDS().

Samples with IDS below ids_cutoff get Status = "Normal" and Mechanism = "ROI". Confidence labels IDS with fixed exploratory screening bands (< 0.1 "High (Normal)", 0.1-0.2 "Low (Normal)", 0.2-0.4 "Moderate (Alteration)", >= 0.4 "High (Alteration)"); the bands do not change with ids_cutoff and are not a measure of statistical certainty. For that, use Status_interval (with n_boot) or calibrate on controls with CalibrateIDS().

Uncertainty

With n_boot > 0, each sample's paternal and maternal deviations are recomputed on resampled probes (see resample), and percentile intervals are reported for IDS (IDS_lower, IDS_upper) and Angle (Angle_lower, Angle_upper, a circular interval around the observed angle, read clockwise from lower to upper). Mechanism_support is the fraction of replicates in the reported Mechanism sector (including "ROI"), a measure of label stability. These are bootstrap uncertainty intervals, not tests. By default they are conditional on the reference: the controls are not resampled, so with few controls they understate the total uncertainty; set resample_reference = TRUE to resample in-cohort controls as well. Because IDS is a distance, its interval never includes 0 and is biased upward for samples near balanced imprinting, so it describes stability and ranking rather than testing against 0; the Angle interval is uninformative when the IDS interval reaches the ROI zone.

With n_perm > 0, origin_perm_p tests whether the sample's deviation depends on the parental-origin annotation, as an imprinting defect does, rather than being shared by all probes. The statistic is the origin contrast |paternal_deviation - maternal_deviation|, which is zero for a shift common to both classes (Global-Hyper, Global-Hypo) and large for single-axis or opposite-axis deviations; the p-value is (1 + #{contrast_perm >= contrast}) / (1 + n_perm) after reassigning the parental labels. IDS itself is not used, because when one class has many more probes, shuffled labels give both classes the majority's deviation. With permute = "probe" correlated probes are exchanged individually, so p-values are anti-conservative. p-values are per sample and not adjusted for multiple testing.

origin_perm_p is interpretable only with a control reference (reference_group, reference_samples or reference_beta). Against the fixed 0.5 reference, normal tissue already deviates slightly, and by different amounts, on the paternal and maternal axes (Infinium probe design, tissue-specific methylation); with hundreds of probes, such a baseline offset alone yields small p-values, so most normal samples would be flagged. With tissue-matched controls the baseline is removed and the test addresses the sample's own departure from it. The bootstrap intervals are meaningful with either reference.
